problem: A particle moves along a straight line relative to a fixed origin $O$ with acceleration, measured in $\text{m}/{\text{s}}^{2},$ given by the function $a(t)=1-2t$, where $t>0$ is the time in seconds. The positive direction is left to right. If the particle has velocity $v=-6\,\text{m}/\text{s}$ when $t=4\,\text{s}$, determine the time intervals in which the particle moves to the right.

activity_context.topic_title: Determining Characteristics of Moving Objects Using Integration

feedback.problem: A particle moves along a straight line relative to a fixed origin $O$ with acceleration, measured in $\text{m}/{\text{s}}^{2},$ given by the function $a(t)=3{t}^{2}-8t+4,$ where $t>0$ is the time in seconds.  The positive direction is left to right. If the particle is stationary when $t=2\,\text{s},$ determine the time intervals in which the particle moves to the right.
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we find $v(t)$ by integrating the acceleration with respect to time:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\int a(t)\text{d}t \\  & =\int (3{t}^{2}-8t+4)\text{d}t \\  & ={t}^{3}-4{t}^{2}+4t+C\end{aligned}
$$

To determine $C$, we use the fact that $v(2)=0.$ Substituting this into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}0 & =(2)^{3}-4(2)^{2}+4(2)+C \\ 0 & =8-16+8+C \\ C & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the velocity $v$ of the particle at time $t$ is $v(t)={t}^{3}-4{t}^{2}+4t.$

To find the time interval in which the particle is moving to the *right*, we must solve the inequality $v>0.$ This gives

$$
{t}^{3}-4{t}^{2}+4t=t(t-2)^{2}>0.
$$

Plotting the graph of $v(t)$, we get the following picture.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14063912/assets/9254ea32fc55b2a703e52f55f4292d9708eef63ae147a9f1d2eac40b85eff319.png)

From the graph, we see that $v>0$ whenever $0<t<2$ or $t>2.$
